h: Making the most of your bounce
p: A little preparation makes a session much more fun. Dress the kids in comfy clothes with no zips, buckles or sharp bits, take off jewellery, and tie back long hair. Have a quick chat before you go in about taking turns on the slides and not bouncing into smaller children, which keeps things safe and stops tears. A bit of a warm-up and a drink before you start are good ideas too.

Parents of very little ones will want to keep an eye on which areas suit their child best, as bigger kids can be boisterous. If you're booking for a party, check the age guidance and any party packages directly, and give yourself time at the start for everyone to arrive and get their socks on.

Burgess Hill makes a handy base for exploring Mid Sussex. Ditchling Beacon, one of the high points of the South Downs, is a short drive away and gives huge views out across the Weald. Wakehurst, Kew's wild botanic garden near Ardingly, is wonderful for woodland walks and the Millennium Seed Bank. Steam fans will love the Bluebell Railway, which runs heritage trains through the countryside between Sheffield Park and East Grinstead. And of course, Brighton's seafront and pier are only around half an hour away if you want to finish the day with fish and chips by the sea.
